title: Sony WH-1000XM6 Review Roundup: Still the Best?
description: Volt’s research-based verdict on Sony’s WH-1000XM6: the class-leading noise cancelling, comfort and calls reviewers praise, plus the price and upgrade catch.
intro: Sony’s flagship noise-cancelling headphones are a refinement rather than a reinvention, and reviewers mostly love them for it.
verdict: Top-tier noise cancelling and comfort. Owners of the XM5 can probably wait.
pros: Comfortable and lightweight, and they fold again
Excellent call quality in most conditions
Long battery life in RTINGS’ testing
cons: Expensive, and a big jump over the XM5’s price
Some smart features are hit and miss
bestFor: Frequent flyers, commuters and anyone who takes lots of calls.
skipIf: You own the XM5 and they still work well, or you want sweat-proof gym headphones.
cardText: Top-tier noise cancelling and comfort; XM5 owners can wait.

sections.h2: Why everyone is talking about it
sections.html: Sony’s 1000X line has been the noise-cancelling benchmark for years, so every new model kicks off a wave of “Sony vs Bose vs AirPods Max” comparison videos.

Expert Reviews called them Sony’s finest headphones yet, and What Hi-Fi called them sensational. TechRadar praised the noise cancelling and comfort. Tom’s Guide and RTINGS were more measured, describing a refinement rather than a big leap. Common complaints: the price, no water resistance, and inconsistent smart features.

If you’re buying your first premium noise-cancelling headphones, these are among the safest picks. If you own the XM5, the improvements are real but small, so look for the older model on sale instead if you’re on a budget.
